title: Case Endings and Dative Subjects
label: ch:ml-dative-case
canDo: I can say that I know Malayalam the way Malayalam itself builds it -- with no subject at all, marking myself with the dative -ikku.

payoff.summary: Say enikkŭ malayāḷaṁ aṟiyāṁ, set it against ñān malayāḷaṁ saṁsārikkunnu, stack the dative's four Dravidian cousins, rebuild pērinŭ and jōlikkŭ and say how -ikkŭ differs from a Latin ending, then point to ക and the soft ര in words you already say.
payoff.note: ML-C06-dative-subject is the chapter's last lesson and assesses all seven atoms it introduces: the dative -ikkŭ and its agglutinative contrast with Latin (ML-C06-dative-ikku), ക and ര (ML-S01-letter-ka, ML-S109-letter-ra, now reached through a prerequisite), and the dative-subject sentence.
